# 2 Samuel Chapter 6 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 173r–174r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_006_page_001.jpg, 2SA_006_page_002.jpg

---

**1** David assembled thirty thousand of Israel's finest men. **2** He set out with his whole company from Baale-judah to bring up the ark of God — the ark that bears the Name, the name of the LORD of Hosts who is enthroned between the cherubim.

**3** They loaded the ark of God onto a brand-new cart and brought it from Abinadab's house on the hill. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the cart — **4** Ahio walking ahead of the ark.

**5** David and the entire house of Israel were dancing wildly before the LORD, with every kind of instrument they could find — lyres, harps, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals.

**6** When they reached the threshing floor of Nachon, the oxen stumbled, and Uzzah reached out and grabbed the ark of God. **7** The LORD's anger blazed against Uzzah. God struck him down right there for his offense, and he died beside the ark of God.

**8** David was furious that the LORD had lashed out at Uzzah. He named that place Perez-uzzah — "the Outburst against Uzzah" — and it is called that to this day.

**9** David was terrified of the LORD that day. "How can the ark of the LORD possibly come to me?" he said.

**10** He refused to bring the ark of the LORD to the City of David. Instead he redirected it to the house of Obed-edom the Gittite. **11** The ark of the LORD stayed in Obed-edom's house for three months, and the LORD blessed Obed-edom and his entire household.

**12** When David was told, "The LORD has blessed Obed-edom's household because of the ark of God," he went joyfully to bring the ark up from Obed-edom's house to the City of David.

**13** When the bearers of the LORD's ark had taken six steps, David sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf. **14** He danced before the LORD with all his might, wearing nothing but a linen ephod. **15** David and all Israel brought the ark of the LORD up with shouts of joy and the blast of trumpets.

**16** As the ark of the LORD entered the City of David, Michal daughter of Saul was watching from a window. She saw King David leaping and spinning before the LORD, and she was filled with contempt for him.

**17** They brought the ark of the LORD inside and set it in its place within the tent David had pitched for it. David offered burnt offerings and fellowship offerings before the LORD. **18** After he finished making his offerings, he blessed the people in the name of the LORD of Hosts. **19** He gave every person in the crowd — every man and woman in Israel — a loaf of bread, a portion of dates, and a raisin cake. Then all the people went home.

**20** When David came home to bless his family, Michal came out to meet him. "What a glorious display the king of Israel put on today!" she said, her voice dripping with scorn. "Stripping down in front of the slave girls of his own servants — like some common exhibitionist!"

**21** David shot back: "I was dancing before the LORD — the LORD who chose me over your father and over his entire house, who appointed me ruler over the LORD's people Israel! I will celebrate before the LORD! **22** I will make myself even lower than this. I may look foolish in your eyes, but those maidservants you're sneering about — they will honor me."

**23** And Michal daughter of Saul had no children to the day she died.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 7 — "for his offense":** The Hebrew *al ha-shal* is one of the most theologically disturbing moments in the narrative. Uzzah reached out instinctively to keep the ark from falling — and God killed him. The narrator offers no justification, no explanation that would satisfy a modern reader. The word *shal* may mean "error," "rashness," or "irreverence," but its exact meaning is unclear. The passage functions as a theological boundary marker: the holiness of God is not safe.

**Verse 14 — "wearing nothing but a linen ephod":** A linen ephod was a priestly garment — essentially a short linen wrap. David stripped off his royal robes and wore only this. It was an act of radical humility before God that Michal read as scandalous public exposure.

**Verse 19 — "dates":** The Hebrew *eshpar* is a hapax legomenon whose exact meaning is debated. It may be a portion of meat, a date cake, or a measure of wine. I render "dates" based on cognate evidence, though "meat portion" is equally defensible.

**Verse 20 — Michal's contempt:** Michal's speech is devastating. She calls David by his title — "the king of Israel" — with acid irony. The word *reyqim* (empty, worthless men) is a social slur. She accuses him of behaving like a nobody. But the narrator has already told us that David was dancing "before the LORD" — so Michal's contempt is ultimately directed at the form of worship itself. Her barrenness (v.23) is the narrative consequence.

**Verse 23 — "had no children":** Whether this is divine punishment, David's deliberate estrangement, or simply narrative consequence is left unstated. The effect is clear: the Saulide line ends with Michal. The daughter of Israel's first king produces no heir. The transition of dynasties is complete.

*— PNEUMA*
